note: Vector-path constants for BW1100 + this DTK. Everything here is either an operator property or a library property; the hardware lives in the hardware profile. ops_per_element is the vector work the operation is defined to do (softmax: max, subtract, exp, accumulate, scale; gelu erf: the erf polynomial plus the gating multiply; tanh-gelu: one polynomial), NOT a fitted number. row_cycles is the per-row block setup and cross-lane reduction, kept in cycles because it is latency rather than arithmetic. efficiency is the calibrated quantity: the fraction of the vector unit the vendor kernel actually reaches, fitted per operator, dtype and regime. Change the hardware profile and the prediction follows the hardware; only efficiency would need re-measuring. row_capacity_elements is where the library stops using softmax_warp_forward (row kept in registers, template parameter log2(R) = 9, 10, 11 for 512, 1024, 2048) and switches to cunn_SoftMaxForwardGmem (row streamed from global memory and read twice, which is what the L1D spill term in vector_ops accounts for). layernorm has its own measurements in both regimes; its warp entry is a fit to a rows sweep at hidden 1024 and 2048 (fixed 411.5 cycles per row plus 0.7485 cycles per element, previously folded into a single per-element slope that put hidden=2048 about 20% too slow), and its fp16 warp row cost is untested. latency_factor is the per-row critical path when rows cannot overlap and is fitted on softmax only; row_latency_factor overrides it per operator, and layernorm measured no such effect (1.0). startup_round_trips is the memory latency exposed once per kernel, in units of hardware.hbm_latency_s, so a machine with slower HBM predictably starts slower without a new constant. fp32 has no reduction measurement, so its reduction constants mirror fp16.
